Definition: to effect thoroughly; specifically, to glean (also figuratively); by implication (in a bad sense) to overdo, i.e. maltreat, be saucy to, pain, impose (also literal)
BiblicalUsage: This word gathers two opposite pictures under one root. In the law it is gleaning, going back over the olive tree and the vineyard so the stranger, the fatherless and the widow can gather what is left. In Exodus it is God dealing with Egypt, showing Pharaoh what He can do to a proud king; the same word covers the harvest left behind and the judgment that strips a nation bare.
TheologicalSignificance: One word doing two jobs carries no single doctrine; its weight is the two pictures side by side, that God leaves enough for the poor and yet deals thoroughly with the proud.
